guide: This is a social travel app: users share albums of places they've been and see travel compatibility with friends and family. It's built with an AI coding assistant and put live with a hosted back end. You need a ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code account, a Supabase project, a Vercel account and a domain.
1. Write one paragraph on what the app does and the two or three features that make it different, such as shared place albums and a compatibility score between friends.
1. Ask Claude Code or ChatGPT (Codex) to build a first version of the app from that paragraph, with sign-up and login.
1. Create a Supabase project for user accounts, albums and places, and ask the assistant to connect the app to it.
1. Deploy the app to Vercel and attach your domain so people can sign up from a real link.
1. Work through the app with a few real people, fix what breaks, and ask the assistant to add the next feature on your list.
1. Share the link and film your progress each day, including the costs and what isn't working yet.
1. Track what you pay each month for hosting, the domain and AI tools, so you know what the app costs before you add paid features.
Watch out: sign-ups and promotion are slower than building, so plan time for getting the app in front of people and keep an eye on the running costs.

```
You are my senior full-stack developer. Build the first version of a social travel app called <app name> where people sign up, create albums of places they have visited, and see a travel compatibility score with friends and family based on shared places. I use <ChatGPT Codex or Claude Code>. I have a Supabase account, a Vercel account and the domain <my domain>.
Please do the following:
1. Propose a simple stack (web app, Supabase for auth and data) and list the tables you need for users, albums, places and friendships.
2. Build sign-up, login, an album page where I can add places and photos, a friends list, and a compatibility page that compares two people's places.
3. Show me how to connect the app to Supabase, keep keys in environment variables, and deploy to Vercel with my domain.
4. Add basic checks so one user cannot see or edit another user's private albums.
Keep it as small as possible and build one feature at a time, stopping for me to test after each. Return the file structure, the code, the exact setup steps, and a list of monthly costs I should expect for hosting, database and domain.
```
